plugins.name: ship-armada
plugins.description: Portfolio-wide orchestrator across every project in ~/Dev — the layer above ship-fleet, and the system prompt for a standing master-orchestrator agent/daemon. Reads the portfolio manifest (~/Dev/ARMADA.md) and ~/Dev/CLAUDE.md, verifies freshness against git, then surveys, plans, routes, and dispatches. Route mode lands a single directive ('research feature X and incorporate it into <project>') in the right project's pipeline — deep research into docs/deep-research, a brief into features-to-triage, an inbox row in the project's ORCHESTRATOR.md that any active fleet picks up (or a new ship-fleet run when approved), and the master manifest updated. Dispatch runs per-repo backlogs through ship-fleet and cross-project rollouts as dependency-ordered campaigns with capped concurrency. Daemon mode proposes on a schedule and executes only what the user has approved.

plugins.name: armada-sync
plugins.description: Keep the portfolio manifest ~/Dev/ARMADA.md truthful after working in any ~/Dev project. Surgical, single-entry updates: status, features, key-file references, updated stamp, index row, one changelog line. The counterpart maintenance skill to ship-armada — every project's CLAUDE.md points here so the manifest stays fresh even when work happens outside the orchestrator.

plugins.name: create-swe-project
plugins.description: create-swe-project (formerly slipway): scaffold a complete, working new project in ~/Dev from a project idea — interview-only LLM, script-made files. Front-loaded interview with inference (modules, RN/Expo vs native SwiftUI, macOS window vs menu-bar AND direct vs Mac-App-Store distribution, codename with 3 options, bundle prefix, GitHub org, design reference, 1Password account+vault), then scaffold.sh renders ~120 templates: pnpm/Turborepo monorepo, Next.js latest with security headers + AI SDK v7 (pinned ^7 on web AND api) + /api/health + syd1 Vercel config, full BP §9 auth (email-code sign-in, JWT + rotating refresh tokens, Resend + React Email templates, dev login gated server-side to non-prod), allowlisted admin console on a separate trust domain, APNs push over HTTP/2 (atlas pattern), optional NestJS (SWC dev/prod parity, jest+@swc/jest), SwiftUI macOS/iOS via XcodeGen with fastlane TestFlight lanes on the App Store Connect API plus sign/notarize/dmg scripts, Expo app (modules only, never EAS) with Maestro flows, Playwright e2e harness, Rust cross-OS core crate, design tokens with drift gate, Caddy + hosts + docker-compose dev env, tsgo typecheck everywhere (never tsc/ts-node), 1Password-seeded .env.local with op:// resolution, git init, install, and the gate run green — then the launch pipeline: background Dossier deep research (read in full, exported to docs/deep-research) grounding seeded feature briefs in features-to-triage, OVERVIEW.md + MARKETING-FEATURES.md with an evidence-based pricing recommendation, comprehensive mocks for every surface/flow/state via design-craft + ux-craft + mac-design-studio with a media-gen-pro icon set and 48px icon audit, a premium GSAP/three.js single-page marketing site held to a zero-slop-tells + Core-Web-Vitals bar with create-luke-content copy and interactive mock slices, and a launch-operations pack (domains, legal drafts scaffolded at /privacy and /terms, App Store kit, analytics schema with motion A/B instrumentation). Includes a referral-loop waitlist module, a region-aware Apple commercialization decision tree, and measured JS budgets from exemplar-site teardowns.

plugins.name: design-review
plugins.description: Expert design and UX review of rendered web apps, websites, app UI flows, infographics and design artifacts — the last pass before a human looks at AI-built UI. Deterministic accessibility, contrast, target-size, performance, motion and layout-integrity gates first (column alignment, shared rails, section gaps, text overlap, dead space, column/band voids, affordance, token overloading); then structural, state, craft, flow and design-system passes against real renders at multiple viewports; then severity-ranked findings with pasteable fixes, evidence, and an explicit statement of what was never checked. Use this whenever someone asks to review, audit, critique, QA, sanity-check or "give feedback on" a UI, page, screen, flow, prototype, landing page, dashboard, deck or design — or says their UI "looks AI-generated", "looks off", "feels cheap", "needs polish", "isn't accessible", or asks whether something is ready to ship. v1.4.0 closes the four blind spots a real 18-surface review found under a fully green oracle set. The runners now scroll the whole document and drain document.getAnimations() before probing and RECORD what was still running: a gate sampled mid-entrance read a #E85A2A accent as #6a2d18 and reported a surface getting worse after a fix that provably removed its failures, and lazy images probed without scrolling report five of eight as broken. probeColumnVoids() adds the column form of dead space that probeDeadSpace() is structurally blind to — a section that renders nothing still occupies its own margins — plus an unfiltered band-seam table, because a page at 92/205/229px ink-to-ink trips no single threshold and is still three-quarters dead space. probeUnconsumedTokens() catches the token declared, emitted and read by no rule: --primary-on-dark was in the contract, set by every record, present in the DOM and consumed by nothing, so a company's own 72px name sat at 2.14:1. Contrast now reports its denominator, <title> is a Level A gate (two route groups shipped without one), and the parity oracle's landmark set is per-page rather than per-site — a checks=904 diffs=0 green sat over a broken grid row on every index page of every tenant because the oracle only ever loaded /. Also: verify the computed value after a CSS fix rather than the presence of the rule, check WHAT rendered rather than THAT something rendered, and treat any first reading of a time- or scroll-dependent property as provisional.

plugins.name: be-my-witness
plugins.description: Validate a UI screenshot against what a test expected and against a design mock, returning a pass/fail gate plus severity-ranked findings. Runs a deterministic pre-scan first (is this evidence, did the surface settle, are the two framings even comparable), crops and zooms rather than judging a full-page thumbnail, looks at every pair in both orders to catch position bias, and classifies each difference as framing, data, structure, styling or state so a changed row count or a different crop cannot fail a build. The test expectation is the oracle; the mock is advisory.

plugins.name: mockup-fidelity
plugins.description: Validate that an implemented React or React Native UI faithfully reproduces a reference mockup, then update the code to close every gap, by measuring the rendered tree rather than eyeballing it or reading source. Treats the mock as the source of truth, inventories every frame including the modals and states the named screens open, and inverts the burden of proof so a difference is a defect until an external citation proves it intentional. Its distinguishing feature is that it refuses to certify a property its browser engine cannot actually measure: a runtime preflight sets each declaration through a real stylesheet rule and reads it back with two different sentinels, and any detector class that fails is reported as inconclusive with the engine's own reason string instead of quietly agreeing. On the sanctioned engine nine classes fail that probe, including box-shadow and placeholder colour, the two properties most often silently wrong. Diffs structure before styling, pairs text-less icons and dividers by bounding box, crops and pixel-diffs every paired element, and emits a present/divergent/absent ledger, a functional-gaps document, and a three-valued exit code where inconclusive is neither a pass nor a failure. Carries a second measurement engine for native macOS, Electron and web-view targets, and for the classes a browser engine reports nothing for: it drives the proctor skill to read the accessibility tree, the compositor's resolved layer values and frame trustworthiness, establishing that engine's own capability tier before a style finding may claim anything. Use it when someone asks whether a build matches its design, to pixel-match a screen, to audit UI fidelity after a port or migration, or to find what a mock contains that was never built.

plugins.name: braindump
plugins.description: Gets everything load-bearing out of a session and onto the page before the context holding it is thrown away. Measured across 121 real compaction events, the built-in prompt keeps 0.3% of the approaches you ruled out and 33.8% of your standing constraints; violations run 0% when a rule survives into the summary and 38% when it does not. Writes a pinned verbatim tier (constraints, corrections, dead ends and exact identifiers) ahead of the narrative, and ships a deterministic retention scorer plus a head-to-head benchmark whose baseline arm is free. Published as compaction-quality until 2026-08.

plugins.name: trawl
plugins.description: Trawl: evidence-grounded parallel divergent ideation for coding agents — cast a wide net over the idea space, then converge on something you can ship. Successor to the original adhd skill. Isolated framed branches, a frozen textbook baseline as both ban-list and boss gate, a balanced frame portfolio with fit floor and apoptosis, mechanism-level convergence with quality floors instead of 1-10 scores, tiered runs (any%/standard/100%) with an auditable receipt line. Every structural change traces to a measured result in the 2024-2026 LLM-ideation literature (see references/evidence.md).

plugins.name: create-mac-icon
plugins.description: macOS app icon creation with a measured fidelity loop: direction catalogue from a 532-icon corpus, three generation engines (hand-authored layered SVG, Arrow vector, corpus-referenced raster), a written audit.html contact sheet, and a multi-scale scoring harness that iterates the SVG master against the winning raster reference until the material matches.

plugins.name: improve-skill
plugins.description: End-to-end skill-improvement pipeline: source skill + user feedback + paid/free Dossier deep-research panel (read in full, citations verified) merged into a plan; the improved skill built as a new plugin; proven with comparative structural evals and a blind multi-family AI judge panel (CLIs + APIs, keys via 1Password); iterated on findings with blind re-judging; then the full brand treatment (user-chosen name and icon concept, mac-design-studio 3-engine icon with audit.html, composed retina banners, Luke-voice README/EVALS with succinct-then-deep comparison, root-README entry) and shipped.

plugins.name: create-skill
plugins.description: Build a brand-new skill from scratch: a broad clarifying interview that pins down trigger, output and done condition before anything is written, paid+free deep research on the skill's domain (read in full, citations verified), the build itself run through skill-creator with every structural choice traced to evidence, proof against a no-skill baseline with structural evals and a blind multi-family judge panel, then the full brand treatment and ship. The sibling of improve-skill, for when there is no predecessor to improve. v1.3.0 hardens the brand phase, which is where this pipeline was quietly skippable: a bundled `render_banner.py` renders banner-src.html and asserts the five things that fail silently (viewport override took effect, web font actually loaded, every image decoded, nothing overflows the frame, PNG is exactly 3200x1040), the marketplace catalogue gate now fails on a missing banner, and the pipeline has answers for three cases it previously had none for: the user forbidding questions, an existing in-repo research corpus that makes a second panel redundant, and a skill that joins an existing plugin rather than getting one of its own.

plugins.name: geminify
plugins.description: Add a Gemini-calibrated `gemini.md` beside an existing skill's SKILL.md, plus the conditional pointer that other models skip, so one skill works on Google's models as well as Claude's. Most skills in an ecosystem are tuned — silently — to whichever model their author ran, and several of their most deliberate decisions are removals: verification scaffolding stripped out because Claude over-verifies when told to double-check. On Gemini those removals leave a vacuum. One measured run showed what fills it: every enumerated requirement delivered (twelve named features, all present) and every categorical one collapsed to a single instance — "all states" → 1, "all menus" → 0, "all flows" → 0 — while the same run wrote itself a review claiming a browser engine that failed on all four invocation attempts and a "100% pass rate on contrast" from a probe that never ran, on an artifact measuring 3.65:1 on every primary button and 1.00:1 on one invisible glyph. So the work is mechanical rather than literary. scan_skill.py reads the target and emits two things: a quota ledger of every categorical quantifier attached to a countable deliverable, and the module triggers — which of nine optional sections the file needs, decided by what the skill demonstrably contains rather than by classifying it as design or not-design, with a three-trigger threshold because single-keyword matching fired seven of eight modules on a skill that renders nothing. Every claim carries its evidence tier ([docs] / [measured-family] / [measured-here] / [derived]) and an explicit unmeasured-on-this-skill list; a docs-only file is legitimate and a measured Gemini run is never required to write one. verify_quotes.py then checks that every quoted [docs] sentence appears verbatim in Google's bundled prompting corpus — it exists because a plausible paraphrase was put in quotation marks and attributed to Google in three separate hand-authored files, and no amount of re-reading caught it. Use whenever someone wants a skill to work on Gemini — "geminify design-craft", "add Gemini support to this skill", "make this skill work in Antigravity", "write a gemini.md for X" — or whenever a skill produced weak output under a Gemini model and the skill itself is not at fault. Not for fixing a skill that is broken for every model (improve-skill), and not for authoring a new one (create-skill).

plugins.name: dossier-report
plugins.description: dossier-report: turn a research question into one published, uniquely-themed HTML page — a Dossier paid+free deep-research panel read in full, compiled into a claim graph, then designed from scratch around its own subject and published to <slug>.fledgeling.app. Ships three readings of the same argument over one claim graph (Primer / Brief / Technical), toggled by the reader, each independently and fully cited from one shared registry and working with JavaScript off, opening with a required TLDR band. Product and buying research also ships a verdict layer: three ranked picks per buyer category plus one overall winner with its cost and its weaknesses, where a paywalled Which?/RTINGS/Choice verdict counts as high-value evidence and every ranking renders as a marked inference. Every page gets its own visual language, light and dark both measured, GSAP as a hard requirement covering micro-interactions and choreography, conditional three.js behind a six-test gate, figures through dataviz in native CSS/DOM, hand-authored SVG or TanStack Charts compiled to static SVG at build time, imagery taken from the research sources with full provenance plus captioned media-gen-pro stills and clips, claim-local citations with source popups, a verified source registry, a measured divider-gutter rule, and the Dossier/Margin marketing chrome. Layout direction comes from a Mobbin trawl with a took/left ledger and /trawl divergence, routed through design-craft and ux-craft.

plugins.name: mac-doctor
plugins.description: Tiered macOS maintenance for a dev machine that agent CLIs, node/dev servers, Docker and Xcode have quietly filled up. Five launchd cadences (15m/1h/12h/1d/7d) whose autonomy widens as the cadence lengthens: short tiers act silently on provably-regenerable debris, long tiers propose and wait. Verification gates before every deletion, a findings ledger that makes recurring leaks visible, and measurement discipline that refuses to total a partial result.

plugins.name: discipline
plugins.description: Session-start operating defaults that cut token spend without cutting task success, tuned for Claude Opus 5 agentic coding. Ships a byte-stable 220-token block for the cached system prefix plus the measured evidence behind every clause, including a paired 106-task benchmark showing that caveman-style response compression cost 7.6 points of task score on Opus 5, with 78% of its apparent saving coming from the agent taking fewer steps rather than writing more tersely.

plugins.name: better-goal
plugins.description: Hold a long autonomous run to a finish line using a Stop guard and a stall watcher this skill creates itself, rather than the built-in /goal. /goal is a prompt Stop hook judged by a small model on transcript text alone, so it grades what the run said rather than what is true, and Claude Code overrides any Stop hook after 8 consecutive blocks while reporting that turn as completed. better-goal (formerly goal-harness) grounds the finish line in the repo's real worklist, writes the brief to docs/goals/goal-<slug>.md, turns "done" into gate commands judged by exit code, preflights the settings that silently end a run, arms a per-slug session-gated command Stop hook, and arms an out-of-band watcher that notices a run dying mid-turn where a Stop hook never fires. It stops deliberately when a gate fails identically turn after turn rather than re-sending the same failure, and answers "has it been met?" and "why did you stop?" from a ledger instead of a guess.

plugins.name: better-loop
plugins.description: Arm recurring or event-driven work as a change-gated watcher this skill creates itself, so a tick fires only when something has actually changed. A scheduled loop re-sends the same unmet condition and the same failing tasks turn after turn, re-billing the session's whole prefix each time: five of twelve measured heavy sessions did exactly that and accounted for 91% of input between them. better-loop (formerly loop-harness) polls a deterministic probe command in the background, wakes the session only on a change and sends the delta rather than the state, backs off on a state it has seen before, holds a wake budget per hour, and can dispatch the tick detached so the session is never woken at all. It picks the mechanism first, preflights the probe for determinism and the skills the tick names, and routes to better-goal when the work has a verifiable finish line. No cron, so no seven-day expiry and nothing left behind in settings.

plugins.name: report
plugins.description: report: turn what a Claude session already worked out into a designed, cited report — one self-contained HTML page that reads as a rich scrolling document and paginates to a clean A4 PDF, plus a one-page TLDR. Ships three readings of the same argument over one claim ledger (Primer / Brief / Technical) that the reader toggles between, each independently and fully cited from one shared registry, working with JavaScript off and selectable per PDF export, opening with a required TLDR section carrying the finding and the ask. Compiles the session's evidence trail into a claim ledger first, so every number carries a locator and anything reasoned is labelled inference — including a comparison's ranked picks, which are inferences by construction, and paywalled lab verdicts, which count as evidence with the paywall stated. Light and dark both ship and both are measured; the PDF is always light. GSAP is a hard requirement on screen, covering micro-interactions and choreography, with an authored static frame keeping all of it out of the ink. Figures go through dataviz in native CSS/DOM, hand-authored SVG or TanStack Charts compiled to static SVG at build time; imagery comes from the evidence trail with full provenance. Layout direction comes from a Mobbin trawl with a took/left ledger, routed through design-craft and ux-craft.

plugins.name: clarify
plugins.description: Decide whether to interrupt the user with a question, then ask it so it takes one click to answer. Sweeps the conversation, the repo and earlier agent output for the answer, kills questions whose answer would not change the work, then refers every surviving technical fork to another model family before the user sees it — fable-5, gpt-5.6-sol, gemini-3.7-flash-high and grok-4.6 at xhigh, a three-family panel for genuinely open forks, and Dossier deep research for questions about the world. A fork whose axis is yours is one you settle and report, not one you ask; what reaches the user is taste, cost, scope, risk and anything irreversible, as one batched AskUserQuestion with two options and no recommendation to nudge them. Treats a note attached to an answer as binding. Ships a deterministic linter that enforces the invariant.

plugins.name: should-compact
plugins.description: Score 0-10 whether NOW is a good moment to compact a coding-agent session, and say why in one line. Scores the BOUNDARY rather than the token count: an open tool chain or a half-finished edit is a hard zero however full the window is, which is the signal that decided 98.07% of holds across 1,089 measured turns. Reads only a hot buffer of recent turns plus an append-only two-tier session log it maintains itself, so it stays cheap enough for Haiku-class models and fast enough to sit in a PreCompact hook — where it can veto an ill-timed automatic compaction, and never vetoes at the wall. Pairs with braindump, handing it the log's verbatim fact tier as grounding.

plugins.name: whats-left
plugins.description: Survey everything a project still needs before its feature set is genuinely complete, and hand it back as one self-contained HTML page: a plain-English status line per item, then an embedded questionnaire that clears every decision waiting on the reader, with pre-selected recommendations, free-text notes and a JSON export. The two halves are one graph, so each blocked item deep-links to the decision that releases it and each decision names how much it actually releases. Separates built from deployed rather than counting both as done, records an untouched default as unconfirmed rather than as an answer, and treats a note attached to an answer as a condition on it. Reads the export back on request and applies each answer, reporting what changed, what could not, and what was deliberately left alone.

plugins.name: proctor
plugins.description: Run a real test campaign against a native macOS app or an iOS Simulator: exploratory sweep, acceptance criteria turned into executable flows, state-matrix and edge coverage, accessibility audit, visual fidelity, determinism measurement, and a report that separates what was proven from what was assumed. Ships with the Proctor MCP server: an unsandboxed launchd agent that reads the accessibility tree and screen contents, and captures through ScreenCaptureKit so every frame carries its own trustworthiness rather than being believed on sight. Actuation runs on Proctor's own process-directed plane by default, so background, occluded and other-Space windows are reachable without stealing focus, and can be delegated to Cua Driver when an operator selects that lane. iOS is a second lane: deep links through simctl and Maestro flow files, scored for determinism. Also ships an embeddable DEBUG reflector that gives apps you own a real computed-style source. Use it when someone asks to test, QA, exercise or find bugs in a Mac or iOS app, whether a flow still works, why a test is flaky, or what breaks in dark mode.

plugins.name: test-campaign
plugins.description: Run a complete UI test campaign against an application and leave behind a living evidence page — coverage, requirements, user-flow storyboards, screenshots, component atlas and defects in one browsable surface where every row has a stable id somebody can point at. Reads the project first — Overview, PRD, feature specs, design md and the latest mock UIs — so the campaign knows what the product *claims* to do before it looks at what it renders, then enumerates the correctness space (surface × state × viewport × theme × role × locale × data shape × modality × execution plane × oracle), samples it deliberately and says so, writes and runs the suite in the project's own harness, sweeps for what no requirement named, and measures the build against its design of record on structure, style, vocabulary and geometry rather than on pixels. Every case carries which rung of oracle it stands on, so a critical flow proved only by "the element exists" fails the gate instead of passing quietly; a case claiming pixels must name a real capture and the channel it came from; a lane claiming the app was running and drawn must name the artifact and what witnessed it attaching, because a suite once reported 100% checked over two desktop apps that had never drawn a window; a published screenshot must name what the capture channel was pointed at, because a wall of 20 captures once showed three unrelated documents while every gate passed and only the filename bound a picture to its surface; a requirement claiming the product acts outside itself — spawning a process, opening a socket, writing a filter rule — must name an independent witness to that effect or be recorded vacuous, because a campaign once armed 220 cases and verified a network policy over a product with no network client in its dependency tree; a check the instrument could not perform is inconclusive rather than clean; armed and unarmed assertions are counted apart; and a coverage ledger's exit code is the verdict, so a partial campaign cannot read as a finished one. Use this when someone asks to test, QA, verify, harden or "prove" a feature or an app, wants e2e or acceptance or visual or accessibility or integration coverage, asks whether something is ready to ship without human testing, wants a test plan generated from requirements, wants user flows discovered and screenshotted, wants to know what is actually covered, or wants a UI to be shown to match its mockups. Spans web, React Native, iOS, and native macOS, Windows and Linux desktop apps, planning each lane to what that lane can actually observe.

plugins.name: anvil-errand
plugins.description: Send a Claude Code agent to work in a container on another machine through Anvil, using the single `anvil errand` verb, and read its refusals correctly when a piece of the path is missing. Covers the whole loop — check the preconditions, start the errand, watch it, stop it — and translates each stable refusal kind (errand_no_node, node_unreachable, image_absent, image_unverified, errand_ticket_unavailable, errand_proxy_unreachable) into the one next step that clears it. Not for setting the path up from nothing: provisioning the node, the engine, the image, the pairing and the proxy is docs/ERRAND_RUNBOOK.md in the anvil repo, which stays the source of record.

plugins.name: shipyard
plugins.description: The shipyard: the feature-delivery stage skills: intake (rough idea to briefs, with trawl ideation and Dossier research), triage (readiness with the Sentinel review and decision-gate assumptions), plan (committed plans plus a comprehensive test strategy), design (all-platform interactive mocks gated by design-review and be-my-witness), work (worktree build through the agy/grok/codex executor lanes with evidence-typed acceptance), verify (cross-family acceptance against the running app - the only path to Done), and gap-fix (the road back from Needs More Work). One tracker adapter covers markdown specs and tasks-MCP boards; shared references carry the model lanes, second-opinion/panel protocol, evidence rules, and the incident ledger.

plugins.name: warrant
plugins.description: Remove the human from per-item software verification by granting a machine a written, tiered authority and revoking it automatically on evidence. Eight skills: charter (the signed warrant, the only human-signed artifact), oracle (source-to-render lineage, tick-and-tie, taxonomy validation — the deterministic plane, built first because the highest-consequence defect is a correctly rendered screen stating a figure no source supports), assay (mutation survival and cannot-fail patterns, because every downstream verdict inherits the suite's fault sensitivity), panel (one out-of-family grader plus orthogonal lens lanes plus an adjudicator that routes disagreement to arithmetic — deliberately not a jury, since nine judges from seven families supply about two effective votes), feedback (escapes become permanent regression cases; calibration from what got missed rather than from a reader study), lot (risk-limited acceptance of a queue, blind to the machine verdict), ratchet (computes earned tiers, applies revocations without asking, and is a plain script because the component deciding a model's authority should not be the model), and ledger (the hash-chained decision record an auditor reads instead of per-item signatures). Grounded in a 22-source panel across four research backends; every rule traces to a claim id in docs/deep-research/claims.json.

plugins.name: ship-feature
plugins.description: End-to-end feature delivery conductor: one feature from rough idea to merged, cross-family-verified production code by conducting the shipyard stages - intake, triage, plan in parallel with design, work, the deferred loop, gap-fix, acceptance-e2e, verify (the only path to Done), and a fail-closed merge with a decided-in-advance rollback. Holds the thread in-session, defers decisions through the second-opinion lanes instead of stalling on questions, and treats every stage artifact as the resumable memory.

plugins.name: ship-fleet
plugins.description: Backlog-wide feature-delivery orchestrator: surveys everything remaining in a repo's pipeline (specs, plans, briefs, mocks, worktrees, deferred follow-ups), writes ORCHESTRATOR.md and a visual hierarchy before any execution, then conducts dependency-ordered ship-feature runners under a global agent budget - with per-item cross-family verification, serialized merges, executor-lane routing, and a ledger a fresh session can resume the whole fleet from.

plugins.name: resume-session
plugins.description: Locate, parse, and resume work from past sessions across any agent CLI (Claude Code, Antigravity/AGY, Cursor, Codex, Grok, or repo workspaces). Discovers sessions by query, ID, path, or recency, extracts the 6D takeover state (original goal, terminal errors, modified files, config keys, decisions, and immediate next steps), and produces an uncorrupted continuity briefing without redundant re-discovery.

plugins.name: tui-craft
plugins.description: Design, mock, build and review terminal user interfaces (TUIs) against a cell grid rather than against source code, because a string template does not tell you how many cells it occupies and that gap is where terminal defects live. Use whenever someone builds, redesigns, reviews or polishes anything that draws to a terminal — dashboard, log viewer, file browser, installer, wizard, admin panel, data browser, or a CLI being turned into a full-screen app — and whenever they name a TUI framework (Bubble Tea, Textual, Ratatui, Ink, Blessed, prompt_toolkit, crossterm, tview, urwid). Also for a terminal UI that "looks broken": torn or missing borders, misaligned columns, text running off the edge, tofu boxes, colours that vanish when piped, breakage on resize. The spine is an instrument: scripts/tui_capture.py drives the running app under a pty at a fixed size, replays its byte stream through a fixture-gated terminal model, and emits a typed frame carrying provenance (command, size, TERM, parser, raw hash); scripts/frame_from_ansi.py produces the same frame from a framework snapshot test, so teatest, TestBackend, Textual run_test and ink-testing-library all feed one set of checks. scripts/tui_gates.py then runs the arithmetic nobody eyeballs correctly — a box that opens and never closes on the same column, a row shoved past its neighbours by a double-width glyph, content that wrapped mid-word off the edge, text cut with no ellipsis to say so, private-use glyphs that need a font the reader may lack, and a frame with no bold and no dim anywhere — each finding located to a row and column. A claim about a screen needs a captured frame: a hand-drawn mock is labelled and may never support a finding, and capture failure is reported as the result rather than papered over by reading the code. On top sits a pattern catalogue traced to 48 shipped TUIs (the border as a metadata shelf, mnemonics marked on the thing they operate, focus signalled twice because a terminal has no hover, the footer as a live surface showing current values, six chart techniques from braille to treemaps) and an anti-pattern list where every entry was observed in a real application. Terminal constraints are cited rather than asserted: NO_COLOR before capability checks, why UAX #11 alone is insufficient and grapheme segmentation is required, OSC 11 to ask the terminal whether it is light or dark instead of assuming, DEC mode 2026 against frame tearing, and gh a11y as the shipped blueprint for an accessible mode. Routes flow, states and the trunk test to ux-craft, hierarchy and restraint to design-craft, and raster comparison to be-my-witness. Not for web or desktop GUI work. Ships two skills: `tui-design` for composing and mocking a screen before the app exists, which compiles a spec into a real frame so cell arithmetic is never counted by hand, and gates the design on a role ladder, colour-independent state and two-channel focus; and `tui-craft` for capturing and gating the running program. Use tui-design whenever someone asks to design, lay out, mock up, wireframe or compare terminal layouts, or asks what a TUI screen should look like, how to lay out panels at 80x24, or how to signal focus and selection. v0.2.1 adds the plugin's banner, composed from the icon's own build constants: the character grid leaves the tile and rules the whole bench at the icon's real cell size, phase-locked to its grid origin.

plugins.name: agent-voice
plugins.description: Give agent-authored text a real voice: the prose an agent emits inside Claude Code and other harnesses. Seven registers, split by who reads the text, because the reader decides the failure mode. Text a person reads (terminal reply, work report, commit and PR, review comment, written document) fails as padding; text a model reads (SKILL.md and instruction files, subagent briefs) fails as ambiguity, and a single set of rules cannot hold both. Both halves are gated by agent_voice_lint.py, which hard-fails closing flourishes, self-congratulation and preamble openers in the human-read registers, and unmeasurable qualifiers, uncounted categorical scope, pressure language and misplaced verification scaffolding in the agent-read ones. Length is a stated rule rather than a disposition, because nothing else controls it: effort governs how much a model thinks rather than how much it says, and sampling parameters are rejected outright on current models, so prose is the only lever. The bound on the whole package is a measurement: a response-compression style on 106 paired agentic tasks cut cost 33.5% and score 7.61 points, with 78% of the saving coming from the agent taking fewer steps rather than writing more tersely, so this skill changes how much gets written and never how much gets done, and uncertainty, risk, security implications and verification that actually happened are content that stays. A dialects layer carries the phrasing each family needs, including the one rule that inverts: Claude Opus 5 self-verifies and its verification instructions are deleted, while a Gemini runner needs the verification step named with its command attached, and one recorded Gemini run satisfied every categorically-named requirement with a single instance ("all states" to 1, "all menus" to 0). Every rule carries a marker naming its evidence, and verify_quotes.py checks each attributed span verbatim against the vendor documents; 82 verify, 0 unverified. Use whenever someone wants agent output to read better ("why are your answers so long", "make this reply shorter", "write the commit message", "tighten this report", "review this SKILL.md", "this prompt is too vague", "rewrite this brief for Gemini", "lint this doc") and before writing any instruction file another model will execute. Not for content written in a person's voice (use that person's content skill, or create-voice-persona to build one), and not for retrofitting a whole skill to another model (use geminify).

plugins.name: design-craft
plugins.description: Design or review a user-facing visual artifact — a landing page, app screen, dashboard, clickable prototype, native mobile mockup, wireframe, variation set, tweakable panel, motion piece, 3D hero, print document, generated imagery or design system — as an opinionated designer rather than a code generator. Roots every hi-fi build in existing context by default and lifts a matched system's resolved values exactly, never rounding them to a 4/8px grid and reporting the rounding as a fix. Names the category's rut and its predictable opposite before generating, derives seven candidates across at least three material families as a probability distribution rather than a best answer, and writes the chosen direction into the artifact as a five-block contract the critique gate then audits promise by promise — because more than a quarter of a generative UI tool's stated design rationales are measured not to appear in what it built. Ships a deterministic gate that computes WCAG contrast from source across hex, rgba, hsl and oklch, follows tokens to their :root definitions, composites opacity, and treats contrast as tri-state: a gradient, image or undeclared ground is reported UNMEASURABLE rather than skipped, since an unmeasured pair and a passing pair otherwise serialise identically. The gate names the silent downstream consequence of every finding, gates on mechanism and warns on fashion, runs markup checks through a real HTML parser, refuses to lint its own documentation, requires a reason on every suppression, proves each of its forty rules can still fire, and prints what it did not check so a clean run cannot be read as verified. Carries a Known limits section measured against the one sanctioned browser, so motion, print, reduced-motion and type fidelity are declared unchecked rather than reported clean — and names the delivery surface's own refusals, because a CDN script inside a published artifact is blocked with no error and the page ships motionless. Thirty phased procedures, per-unit critique gates with a computed disposition, an autonomous mode, and a standing pairing with ux-craft for flows, forms and UX review.

plugins.name: ux-craft
plugins.description: Book-grounded UX engine for building, mocking and reviewing web and mobile UIs, forms, flows and emails — the UX brain that pairs with design-craft's visual hands. Three modes (Build / Review / Advise) over eleven references, and a deterministic gate that refuses what prose only asks: stdlib-only ux-lint.py runs static over HTML/JSX/CSS and probes a rendered page through Obscura, with every finding naming what you did, what the user silently gets, and the fix. Only exit 0 is a pass — a run that examined zero files refuses rather than reporting a clean sheet, and every run prints a never-empty not-checked list, because a check that cannot measure must say so instead of reporting zero. v2 resolves the accessibility floor against the standards themselves: 24x24 CSS px is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 at AA and is the only target-size number a WCAG failure may cite, 44x44 CSS px is SC 2.5.5 at AAA, and Apple's 44pt and Android's 48dp are craft targets in density-independent units that are not WCAG numbers at all. Twelve non-negotiables each carry the silent symptom that appears when they break, the state grid is a counted artifact rather than a rule that was read, and the destructive-action gate table, the probe-honesty rule and the model-family evidence taxonomy are available to every model rather than quarantined behind a model check. Carries a Known limits section, an evidence file rating the replication status of every behavioural law it cites (including the ones it argues against), the measured blind spots of the only sanctioned browser, and an autonomous-mode carve-out so a pipeline run is not told both to ask and not to ask.

plugins.name: deck-craft
plugins.description: Build, review or convert a slide deck across three targets from one body of craft: a self-contained fixed-stage HTML presentation, lecturn.deck/1 JSON with a .pptx round-trip, or an investor deck assembled from a bundled library of 200 slide layouts in 27 families and 21 recipes. Carries its own design layer rather than depending on a general design skill — a supplied DESIGN.md or token file is binding, a direction is authored on three named axes when no brand exists, and type is sized from a viewing-angle derivation rather than from web habit. Deck-specific narrative discipline: the title sequence written before any slide because the titles read in order are the argument, speaking-versus-reading density as an explicit fork, one idea per slide, and a named slide count treated as a contract. Ships a deterministic preflight gate that runs in a headless browser and is built to be unable to pass silently: the probe carries its own blocker and warning policy plus a stated consequence for every finding, refuses a config key it does not recognise, and echoes its configuration back so the runner can prove the settings that were asked for actually arrived. Only exit 0 is a pass — a probe that returned nothing, a config that never landed, a check that threw and a run that examined zero slides each get their own code and their own refusal. Regulated decks add per-slide disclosure checks sourced to SEC Regulation G and Item 10(e), the December 2022 Compliance and Disclosure Interpretations on equal-or-greater prominence, and ASIC RG 230; chart integrity covers truncated baselines, dual axes and inverted axes; and given the source document it cross-checks every figure on the deck against it, because fabrication arrives as texture around a real number rather than as an invented headline.

plugins.name: mac-craft
plugins.description: Design and review authentically native macOS application interfaces — mock windows as self-contained HTML/CSS or a token-precise spec, with a committed aesthetic direction, a state matrix, a token table an implementer can build from, and a deterministic gate that computes contrast instead of asserting it. Grounded in Apple's macOS UI kit deconstructed to exact (specified) values, the published HIG, an August 2026 four-backend research panel across 110 sources, and taste learned from 135 curated macOS apps. Ships scripts/mock_check.py: WCAG contrast computed from the declared cascade across light, dark and increased-contrast contexts with alpha compositing; a metric block cross-checked against both the kit and the stylesheet; keyboard, token-discipline, casing, cursor, self-containment, content and artifact-naming checks. It exits 2 rather than 0 when a check cannot be performed, because examined=0 is a gate that never ran. Replaces mac-design-studio and answers to that name. App icons are not designed here — they route to create-mac-icon.

plugins.name: mac-design-digest
plugins.description: Incrementally digest macOS app UI screenshots, app icons, and official Apple UI kits into a persistent design corpus — per-app token profiles, cross-app pattern entries, aesthetic style clusters, icon anatomy digests, and a master TASTE.md — where every value carries a provenance mark from a closed set and every written file is checked by an executable gate before the run is reported done. Ships corpus_check.py (twelve checks over seventeen named invariants over the written corpus — ledger integrity and append-only rows, every ledger target existing, cross-app patterns recorded, the 3-independent-apps canon bar, the native-lineage gate, canon traceability, cluster contradiction budget, placeholders, dated and levelled headers, non-empty knowledge gaps below Proficient, one mark per axis with a composed pair where the row's role needs both, the app count a (recurring)/(canon) mark claims, and a pinned precision baseline so a value cannot silently gain precision it never earned) and sketch_extract.py (reads .sketch archive JSON in memory, derives the control ladder from symbol frames, classifies capsule radii by geometry rather than by an undocumented sentinel, and flags instruction-shaped strings it reads out of the archive). Use whenever the user provides mac app screenshots or icons and wants to digest, study, learn from, analyze, or add to the corpus — and when ingesting a Figma or Sketch UI kit export. Routes generation out: mocks to mac-craft, icons to create-mac-icon.

plugins.name: generate-investor-portal
plugins.description: Generate a complete investor-portal record — theme tokens, section content, provenance-marked figures, imagery and motion — into a database from a company's DESIGN.md and a crawled company overview, so a new company is a generated record rather than new code and one generic renderer serves it at that company's own subdomain. Its distinguishing feature is that it ships the gate instead of describing it: assets/record-gate.mjs runs 600+ record-level checks with no server, no database and no network, and refuses the write rather than the read, so a rule added to it can never take a live portal down. The check that matters most is that a figure is not allowed to live in prose — a currency amount, a percentage or a date in any prose slot without a provenance object around it is refused, because that is the channel a plausible fabricated number actually arrives through, and a missing figure has to become a visibly marked unavailable state with a reason code instead. It treats the crawled overview as untrusted third-party content and carries a verbatim injection fence into every subagent brief and every paid image prompt; it refuses a republish before anything is crawled or generated rather than after; it measures accent contrast arithmetically on hex against role-aware floors so a brand colour is never rejected where it belongs; and it detects the defect no per-tenant gate can see, two companies publishing the same portal, by comparing three collision keys against the published peer set. Use it when someone wants an investor portal built, generated or refreshed for a company, wants a company onboarded onto a portal platform, or hands over a DESIGN.md plus a company overview and asks for a portal from them.

plugins.name: stocktake
plugins.description: Count what a tracker board claims against what the codebase actually holds, card by card, and move each one to the column its evidence supports. Reads every comment and attached image and rebuilds the numbered requirement list from the ticket BEFORE opening any completion record or diff, because a diff read first supplies the frame and the requirements it silently dropped never enter the list. Locates the work — merged, on a branch nobody merged, unpushed, in a worktree, or never built — then traces each requirement to the code that PRODUCES its value rather than to a surface that renders it, and judges whether the tests standing behind it could actually fail: which rung of oracle each critical requirement stands on, armed and unarmed assertions counted apart, a denominator for what the gate really runs. Grades every verdict out of family with a single strongest judge rather than a panel, because nine frontier judges across seven families supply about two independent votes. An inconclusive result blocks and never rounds up to a pass. Cards with work left get a brief written for ship-fleet to orchestrate; cards with open decisions get referred to another model family or decided with a named recommendation rather than parked on the reader; cards whose evidence holds are promoted to Done — and never past it into a human's column until eight named preconditions hold for one pre-registered low-risk class, which a bundled gate refuses by default. Use whenever someone asks to triage, sweep, review, reconcile or clean up a board or backlog, asks what is left across a set of tickets, asks whether items in a review column are genuinely done, asks which tickets sit in the wrong status, or says a column has piled up. At Done, the column a card may reach is decided by the `warrant` plugin rather than by a checklist: warrant_column.py reads the signed warrant and the ratchet's last word and returns Verified where the card's defect class has earned warrant tier 3 with no revocation, Needs More Work where a warrant gate failed on the card's own evidence, and Done with every reason named otherwise. A grant states the substitution it rests on every time, because a warrant tier is earned by absence of escapes rather than by a measured non-inferiority study, and the signed warrant is a person accepting that in advance.

plugins.name: vouch
plugins.description: Reconcile and substantiate a personal-expense reimbursement claim end to end, repeatably. Vouching is the audit term for tracing a record back to its source document, and that is the whole skill: every claimed charge is keyed to the supplier's own invoice, and every invoice is read for the account it was issued to. Sweeps a personal-accounting MCP (PocketSmith or any equivalent), the Apple Mail index via the Sift MCP, card statement PDFs and a downloads folder; detects the days where the bank feed is silent and backfills them from statements, which is where the charges nobody noticed are hiding. Decides each row on three gates the operator supplies: the invoice must name a company account, the payment must land on a card the claimant owns personally, and the charge must be absent from the prior claim. Drives supplier portals through proctor when a login is needed, and hands back a wanted-invoices page listing date, supplier, estimated amount, portal link and account address whenever a portal refuses automation. Emits a claim CSV matching the employer's own form, invoices filed by month and named for the invoice number printed inside them, and two unbranded reports, one for the manager approving payment and one for the accountant checking GST. Ships a gate suite that fails on arithmetic, sign convention, date range, duplicate invoice numbers, orphan files and any filename that disagrees with its document. Use whenever someone asks to prepare, reconcile, substantiate or check an expense claim or reimbursement, asks which invoices are still missing, or runs the monthly claim.

plugins.name: atlas-publish
plugins.description: Takes the open PRs of the Atlas/Bella monorepo to a registered draft release on either the over-the-air or the App Store lane, classifying between them from the expo-updates native fingerprint rather than from intent — ios.buildNumber sits inside that fingerprint, so a buildNumber bump alone forces a store release. Every irreversible step names the observable to read back, because a build tool, an upload and an MCP call all return success without having done anything. Gates report not-run as a third state beside passed and failed, which is how a cert-parity test that skips its only real assertion stops reading as a green gate. Eleven steps, each marked with the lanes it applies to and each with an abort path next to it. Draft is where automation stops: publishing to users is a founder action the skill will not take. The diff review that used to ship beside it is now the standalone code-review plugin.

plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: A diff review that reports what it could not check. Finds with fourteen named angles that are forbidden from suppressing each other, so two reasons for flagging one line both survive to be judged; verifies with three verdicts, where realistic-but-unproven stays in as PLAUSIBLE rather than being dropped with the noise, and only REFUTED leaves; then closes with a coverage ledger naming every angle, checklist and gate that never ran, and why. Learns the target repository at runtime rather than carrying a hard-coded project map — gate commands from the package scripts and CI config, frameworks from the installed dependency versions, global controls and cross-package boundaries by grep — so a candidate naming a framework the repo does not install is refuted from evidence rather than from a constant somebody wrote into a skill. Three depths, each printing its own budget line at the top of the report so what ran is visible rather than inferred; areas and ten focus lenses that compose; checklists for TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS, React Native, frontend/web, security and logic bugs, routed by path and lens; sharding above a size threshold with the fan-out reconciled against the bucket list, because a harness that loses an agent reports the wave complete. One verifier vote rather than a judge panel, on the measurement that panels saturate at about two effective votes. Read-only on source: it reports findings and does not apply fixes. Carries a token-light prepush gate on the outgoing diff.

plugins.name: email-digest
plugins.description: Build a recurring multi-item digest or roundup email that survives contact with real inboxes: a tiered layout that absorbs volume instead of capping it, a table-based render that works in Outlook's Word engine and with images blocked, and a deterministic gate carrying every rule back to the evidence behind it. Refuses the two fixes people reach for first, because the measured evidence goes the other way.

plugins.name: recover-claude-code
plugins.description: Bring back Claude Code sessions, workflows and subagents that a crash interrupted, with the context they already had instead of restarting them from scratch. Use after a terminal, Ghostty or machine crash, a force-quit, or a jetsam/out-of-memory kill took sessions down, and whenever a previous recovery cold-started fresh agents and lost what they had already worked out. Separates the genuinely dead sessions from the still-running ones using the live-session registry at ~/.claude/sessions (a pid-keyed record carrying sessionId, cwd, peer name and status), because the two probes that look correct both fail: ps output never contains the session id, and the scratchpad directory is named by a per-process id that stops matching once a session has been resumed. Reopens each dead session in its own Ghostty tab at its original working directory under its original session id (never --fork-session, which orphans every workflow journal it is trying to reach), handing over a brief as a positional prompt so the session wakes up knowing it crashed rather than auto-submitting "Continue from where you left off". Restores interrupted work by promoting a dead subagent's sidechain transcript into a resumable session so it keeps the files it read and the findings it closed, rather than replaying its prompt into a blank context; measured, a promoted transcript named its item, branch and a closed finding from memory. Finds a run's persisted script by run id across every project directory, because Claude Code files the script under the project directory of the live working directory and the journal under the original one, so any session working in a worktree splits its own state in two and a snapshot-only lookup reports no script for precisely the runs that need recovering. Offers a journal splice for a long completed prefix that resumeFromRunId would otherwise re-run (the cache miss is sticky, so the interrupted agent is the first miss and every later call re-runs, including ones already committed), and refuses to fabricate a result line. Ships a read-only scanner, a transcript promoter, a Ghostty tab driver with a dry run, a splice tool that only ever writes a copy, and a fixture-based self-test. Sibling of workflow-resume, which handles the opposite failure: a run that reported completed while losing agents to API errors.

plugins.name: defer
plugins.description: Decide which model a piece of work goes to, and produce the exact command that sends it there. One routing policy for every skill that hands work outside the session: six task classes mapped to seven lanes across five model families, each pinned to a model and an effort, with the CLI arguments, the environment GLM needs, and the check that proves the lane ran as routed. Where several lanes are eligible it picks the one with the most plan headroom per remaining day, measured — Claude and Codex report a real utilization percentage that is already on disk, and Grok, GLM and Gemini are counted locally against a budget calibrated from a percentage you can see. Ships a lane prober, a policy selftest that runs no model, and a wire-verify method per lane, because the most expensive failure in a multi-model system is a plausible answer from the wrong one.
